title: Time Signature
principle: Short-short-long motif, tactile clock onset, low-roughness celeste body.
why: The clearest brand mnemonic: fast, elegant, and easy to recognize after a few repetitions.

title: Ruby Celeste
principle: Warm paper transient plus bright but restrained upper partials.
why: Feels more crafted and less app-generic while staying gentle enough for repeated use.

title: Paper Tile
principle: Auditory-icon texture paired with an abstract resolving motif.
why: Connects the sound to supertime's paper/ink puzzle surfaces without literal nostalgia.

title: Dawn Resolve
principle: Slower attack and warm lower partials reduce interruption cost.
why: Good if the daily notification should feel inviting rather than task-like.

title: Solved Stamp
principle: Clear onset, stronger cadence, and a little haptic weight.
why: Confident enough for wins and streaks without becoming an alarm.

title: Group Glint
principle: Call-and-response spatial pings increase discriminability.
why: Reads as social activity while avoiding common chat-app cadences.

title: Tomorrow Bell
principle: Descending air gesture into open bell lowers perceived urgency.
why: Useful for a gentle 'new puzzle is waiting' moment.

title: Focus Margin
principle: Minimal two-note earcon with very low RMS and short decay.
why: Best for people who dislike prominent custom notification sounds.

title: Daily Arc
principle: Gentle rising pitch cue creates orientation without urgency.
why: Has motion and optimism, but less sparkle than a game-completion cue.

title: Morning Check
principle: Stable motif plus tiny paper close anchors the daily ritual.
why: Feels like a habit marker rather than a message alert.

title: Ink Ping
principle: Single distinctive timbre with controlled high-frequency sparkle.
why: A strong option if the sound must be extremely short but identifiable.

title: Warm Win
principle: Compact rising motif with mild echo to improve memorability.
why: More playful than the lead candidate but still polished.

title: Thread Reply
principle: Repeated pitch creates conversation semantics without speech.
why: Useful for later social features where a reply should sound distinct.

title: Streak Seal
principle: Lower transient plus stepwise resolution conveys completion.
why: A little more ceremonial, best for solved/streak states.

title: Invite Spark
principle: Whoosh-plus-pairing makes the cue distinct from reminders.
why: Feels like something arrived from another person, not a timer.

title: Calendar Lift
principle: Clock ticks plus warm bell map directly to time without alarm harshness.
why: The most literal 'time' cue in the set.

title: Glass Route
principle: Fast contour and airy onset balance attention with elegance.
why: Most 'app-like' in the positive sense: clean, modern, and kinetic.

title: Polite Alert
principle: Sharper onset and wider interval raise detectability without repetition.
why: For a reminder that needs to cut through, but not feel like a warning.

title: Game Room
principle: Tactile object sounds increase semantic fit and memorability.
why: More playful and physical, good if the brand should lean game-first.

title: Ruby Finish
principle: Three-note upward resolve with stronger product-sound weight.
why: The most memorable alternate if the lead candidate feels too understated.
